decisions.reason: Message 138 independently clarifies the Hero V and É accent peak alignment, and that clarification is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY. The second V hierarchy change requires no further edit.
Using the E and L cap height as a reference for the second V does not change the required geometry, terminals, or architectural language of the E and L letterforms.
The second V's new height hierarchy and quiet-echo role do not alter the shared terminal treatment or its evaluation rules.
The Hero V is only a fixed visual-height reference for the second V; message 138 does not change the Hero V's geometry or existing attributes.
Message 138 changes the independently modeled visual hierarchy and placement of the second V, not its glyph derivation or right-arm geometry.

The second V hierarchy refinement does not change the requirement that the É accent be literally derived from the approved Hero V terminal. Peak alignment is handled by a separate candidate Requirement.
Changing the second V's vertical hierarchy does not necessarily alter the wordmark's horizontal kerning or unified-reading requirement.
The typography hierarchy refinement has no entailed effect on the deferred champagne material treatment.
The source provides design feedback but does not change the separate obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
The second V hierarchy decision is unrelated to proof attachment formats or Mac viewability.
